items.title: Expired Stellar challenges and OAuth states are never pruned from memory
items.description: ## Context The auth module keeps pending Stellar challenges and OAuth states in memory (`apps/api/src/auth.ts:387-391`: `pendingStates` / `pendingChallenges` maps). Challenge issuance is rate-limited per IP, but nothing ever removes stale entries. Verified at baseline `fbbe7e3` (main). ## Problem `pendingChallenges` entries are never deleted — not on expiry, not on failed verify — and expired OAuth states linger too: - `auth.ts:624` — `pendingChallenges.set` on every `/auth/stellar/challenge`. - `auth.ts:648-652` — an expired / invalid verify returns `401` without deleting the entry; only success marks `used = true`. - `auth.ts:718` — `pendingStates.set` with a 10-minute expiry, vs `:739` where it is deleted only when the callback runs. No sweep timer or size cap exists for either map (contrast `SlidingWindowRateLimiter`, which has `maxKeys` + eviction). Both maps grow unboundedly in a long-lived process, and an attacker can mint challenge entries indefinitely over time despite the per-minute rate limit. ## Contributor Task Prune expired entries from both maps and delete challenge entries on failed verification. ## Deliverables - Delete the challenge entry on expired / invalid verify. - Periodic (or on-issue) pruning of expired entries from both `pendingChallenges` and `pendingStates`. - A test asserting that repeated challenge issuance + expiry does not grow retained state. ## Dependencies None blocking. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A failed / expired verify removes the challenge entry. - [ ] Expired OAuth states do not accumulate after their 10-minute TTL. - [ ] Repeated challenge issuance over time keeps retained state bounded. - [ ] Successful challenge / OAuth flows are unchanged. - [ ] `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` all pass. ## Verification ## Proof of Completion - Link the new pruning test and its passing output. - Show retained map size before / after expiry in the test. ## Out of Scope - Moving challenges to a shared / persistent store (documented as a future upgrade path in `auth.ts:27`). - Changing challenge or OAuth TTLs. ## Non-negotiable Constraints - No change to the challenge / verify success path. - No new dependency. - Pruning must not delete a still-valid, still-usable entry. ## PR Requirements - One PR, scoped to this issue. - Reference this issue in the PR description. - Include the bounded-state test.

items.title: K4: prompts through kubed-mcp's command_reader
items.description: ### Existing requests - [x] I searched the open issues and this isn't already requested. ### Problem / motivation kb reads commands in its own dialects, with elicitation and a free-text argument (`catalogue/prompts/`, `MCPFilePrompt`, `PromptProvider`, `_load_prompts`, `PromptRow`), beside the plugin layer. kubed-io/quick-mcp#19 adds `mcp.command_reader(fn)` and the first-segment prefix, so kb's dialects plug into the plugin layer. ### Proposed solution - kb's dialect reader becomes its `command_reader`. - Delete `PromptProvider`, `_load_prompts`, `PromptRow` and the prompt claims. - Names keep PRM-41 and PRM-44 through the first-segment prefix (PLUG-63). **Done when** - kb's live dump (ten scopes, with and without `kb+`) differs from the one before this change only by the changes this issue names. Every prompt's name, arguments and rendered text are unchanged. ### Alternatives considered - **Keep `PromptProvider`.** It duplicates the plugin layer's scoping and naming. ### Anything else? - Needs kubed-io/quick-mcp#19, and K3 (#79) first. — Claude, for Dr K 🗒️ Agent notes · 2026-11-24 05:25 UTC ## #82: K4, prompts through kubed-mcp's command_reader (sub-issue 3 of epic #80) **What is asked.** kb's dialect reader becomes its `mcp.command_reader(fn)` (quick-mcp#19). Delete `PromptProvider`, `_load_prompts`, `PromptRow` and the prompt claims. PRM-41 and PRM-44 names hold through PLUG-63's first-segment prefix. Done when: the live dump over ten scopes, with and without `kb+`, differs only by named changes, and every prompt's name, arguments and rendered text are unchanged. Keeping `PromptProvider` was ruled out because it duplicates the plugin layer's scoping and naming. **Order.** After K3 (#79) and #81 (prefix). Needs the kubed-mcp release carrying #19, which lands after #18 and #28 in quick-mcp; #19's approval waits for #18 and #28 to merge into `issue-16`. Before #83 (agents), #84 (index and /health), #86 (mirror tools, `X-MCP-Prompts` withdrawn). **Already ruled (on quick-mcp#19):** - The reader is `fn(text, path, name, plugin)`. It returns a FastMCP `Prompt`, or a string giving the skip reason. - The reader runs once on the raw text when the plugin is read, then once per build on the rewritten text. With no rewriters, the first result is reused. - Builds never read the disk; a kept last-good plugin serves its own bytes. - Reader errors (`OSError`, `ValueError`, `yaml.YAMLError`) become skips in `Plugin.skipped` (PLUG-25), logged as `prompt is skipped: `.

items.title: Bildschirm: Spiegelung und echten Zweitmonitor auf Telefon oder Tablet ergänzen
items.description: ## Verbindliche Nutzerentscheidung zum Release und zur Oberfläche **Neueste Nutzeranweisung: jetzt in den aktuellen Arbeitsumfang (#113) aufgenommen.** Die vorherige Release-Zurückstellung von #244, #245 und #246 ist aufgehoben. Oberflächeneinstieg unter **KDE Connect → Erweiterte Funktionen**; tatsächliche Implementierung und eigene native Abnahme erforderlich. Zuerst die gemeldeten Fehler der laufenden Nutzerprobe korrigieren. Veröffentlichung weiterhin erst nach neuem Nutzer-Okay und den verbindlichen Systemstarttests. Geplante Erweiterung aus dem Linksy-Vergleich #233: **Bildschirmspiegelung und ein echter zusätzlicher Monitor auf Telefon/Tablet**. Referenz: Linksy [Sessionverwaltung](https://github.com/LinkSy-mg/linksy-desktop/blob/e2c8970413f8547ff3d85e84b4757e33837b5a22/crates/linksyd/src/sessions.rs), [ScreenCast-/RemoteDesktop-Portaladapter](https://github.com/LinkSy-mg/linksy-desktop/blob/e2c8970413f8547ff3d85e84b4757e33837b5a22/crates/linksy-screen/src/portal.rs) und [Android-Anzeige](https://github.com/LinkSy-mg/linksy-mobile/blob/3095bbb52badb880d8e8cb037c353a71027f393c/lib/features/sharing/display_screen.dart). **Vorhandener Anknüpfungspunkt:** Magnolie hat native KDE-Eingabe-, Präsentations- und Digitizerpfade (#149/#153/#168). Das Zeichenblatt bleibt eine dokumentgebundene Anwendung; ein zusätzlicher Desktopmonitor und laufende Bildschirmübertragung erhalten einen eigenen Sitzungsvertrag. **Kompatibler Entwurf und Abnahme:** - Bildschirm ansehen, Bildschirm steuern und virtuellen Monitor als getrennte Fähigkeiten/Einwilligungen behandeln; tatsächliche Plattform-/Compositorfähigkeit ermitteln. - Auf Linux vorhandene ScreenCast-/RemoteDesktop-Portale verwenden; virtuelle Ausgänge nur während der verhandelten Sitzung anlegen und bei Ende entfernen. Windows-Unterstützung nativ und gesondert bestimmen. - Seitenverhältnis, Rotation, Auflösung und Eingabekoordinaten der Gegenstelle verhandeln; bestehende native Eingabehandler weiterverwenden. - Begrenzter Medienkanal, genaue aktive Geräte-/Schlüssel-/Sitzungsidentität und geordnete Behandlung von Abbruch, Widerruf und spätem Eingang. - Native Prüfung mit tatsächlicher Anzeige und geeigneten Plattformen: sichtbare Übertragung, echte zusätzliche Monitorfläche, präzise Eingabe und vollständiger Aufräumnachweis nach Ende/Fehler. Die bestehende Zeichenblatt-Initialisierung aus #168 und die übrigen aktuellen Integrationsaufträge behalten ihren konkreten Umfang. Diese Erweiterung wird eigenständig umgese

items.title: 카카오 매장 메뉴 영양성분 추정: 메뉴명 정규화 단위 LLM 추정과 /restaurant/detail 연동
items.description: ## 배경 카카오로 수집한 매장 메뉴(`restaurant_branch_menu`, 운영 1,134,585행, 지점 66,814곳)에는 메뉴명과 사진 URL만 있고 영양정보가 없다. 그래서 개인 식당은 `/restaurant/detail`의 칼로리·추천 탭(균형·저칼로리·단백질)에 쓸 수 없다(#39에서 `/brands`가 개인 식당을 `restaurant_id: null`로 돌려주지만 앱은 null이면 메뉴를 부르지 않는다). 행 단위로 추정하면 비용·시간이 크지만, 메뉴명을 정규화하면 182,224종으로 줄고 5곳 이상 매장에 있는 20,161종이 행의 80%를 덮는다(분석 기준: 메인 체크아웃 `kakao-map/*구/menus.csv`). ## 근거 문서·데이터 - `docs/restaurant-nutrition-estimation-protocol.md` (하이브리드 RAG, confidence 기준, 미관측 브랜드 MAE 약 104~126kcal) - `benchmark-results/restaurant-nutrition-cost-throughput-summary.md` (`gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, 10개 묶음 메뉴당 입력 332/출력 69토큰, $0.0000607, Batch API $0.0000304) - `benchmark-results/foodbd-photo-effect.json` (사진 추가 시 칼로리 MAE 247.5→238.2, ±30% 13.7%→11.0%, 지연 2배) - `docs/restaurant-nutrition-prompt-data-boundary.md`, `docs/kakao-restaurant-branch-import.md` - `scripts/*restaurant-nutrition*`, `src/utils/menu-name.util` ## 비용·시간 추정(10/18 단가 기준, 이미지·재시도 제외) | 범위 | 일반 호출(10개 묶음) | Batch API | 시간(동시 5개 이론값) | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 상위 2만 종(행 80%) | 약 $1.2 | 약 $0.6 | 약 15분 | | 전체 18만 종 | 약 $11 | 약 $5.5 | 약 2시간 10분 | | 중복 제거 없이 113만 행 | 약 $69 | 약 $34 | 약 13시간 | ## 할 일 1. 메뉴명 정규화 단위 추정 결과를 저장할 테이블과 TypeORM 마이그레이션(운영 적용은 메인 세션이 허락 후). - 정규화 메뉴명(UNIQUE), 칼로리·탄수화물·단백질·지방·당·포화지방(기존 응답 필드에 맞춤), 기준 중량, confidence, 출처(`mfds` 정확 일치 / `llm`), 모델·프롬프트 버전, 근거 메뉴, 토큰 수, 생성 시각. - 매장 메뉴는 정규화 메뉴명으로 연결(재수집해도 이미 추정한 이름은 다시 호출하지 않음). 2. 추정 스크립트(`scripts/`): 대상 메뉴명 추출(빈도순, `--limit`) → 식약처 음식명 정확 일치는 LLM 없이 기준값 → 나머지는 프로토콜의 RAG 근거와 함께 10개 묶음으로 Gemini 호출 → 결과 파일(JSONL) 출력 → 별도 단계로 DB 적재. 재시작 가능(이미 처리한 이름 건너뜀), 동시성·속도 제한·재시도 옵션, `--dry-run`(호출 없이 대상·예상 토큰만 출력). Gemini는 `GeminiClient` 뒤에 두고 `FakeGeminiClient`로 테스트. 3. 시범 평가 방법: 식약처 정확 일치 메뉴와 공식 브랜드 메뉴(브랜드 연결 지점)를 정답으로 표본 오차(MAE, ±30% 비율, 보류 비율) 산출 스크립트. 4. `/restaurant/detail` 연동(백엔드만으로 개인 식당 메뉴 노출): `/brands`에서 개인 식당에 가상 `restaurant_id`(예: 100000000 + 지점 ID)를 주고, `/detail`이 그 범위를 받으면 지점 메뉴 + 추정 영양값을 기존 응답 형식으로 돌려준다. API 계약 스냅샷 확인 필수. ## 실행 경계 - 스크립트 작성·테스트는 worktree 세션, 실제 Gemini 호출·운영 DB 조회·적재·마이그레이션은 메인 체크아웃 세션. - 외부 API 호출·대량 적재는 사용자 명시적 허락 후에만 실행한다.

items.title: OpenSmash.Avalonia doesn't pull new GitHub commits for updates, takes multiple tries to get it to launch properly, doesn't have an app icon, should replace Play SSBU as new way to launch/play (MacOS)
items.description: ### What would you like? OpenSmash.Avalonia takes precedence over OpenSmash.Launcher and Play SSBU for updating/playing OpenSmash-Ultimate after building with v0.4.1. On MacOS (maybe other OS' as well), OpenSmash.Avalonia doesn't have an app icon and takes multiple tries to properly get it to launch. When it does launch, signing into and linking a SSBU Arena account works. Because OpenSmash.Avalonia is taking precedence over Play SSBU and other launchers, it should be what gets put into /Users/x/Applications instead of the current Play SSBU. Setting up OpenSmash.Avalonia and trying to launch Play SSBU after the fact from /Users/x/Applications results in not showing any kind of signed in state, requiring the launch to happen from OpenSmash.Avalonia itself. This renders Play SSBU practically obsolete and can cause confusion on where to launch OpenSmash-Ultimate from. Additionally when using the previous Install WindowSmash.command or OpenSmash.Launcher build/update options, they pulled and installed any and all GitHub commits that got pushed out. OpenSmash.Avalonia is not capable of this and as a result every update requires a complete re-install of the from the Code -> Download ZIP option on OpenSmash-Ultimate GitHub, at least on MacOS. ### Alternatives or examples _No response_

items.title: Keep session content out of logs with a content-free logging helper
items.description: ## Description Every service needs one way to log that cannot leak session content. RC-03 forbids keeping audio, transcripts, excerpts or narrative feedback anywhere at rest, and that includes logs. The likely leak paths in this stack are request-body logging, error messages that echo a turn, and tracebacks (Implementation Plan IR-5). This Issue adds a shared structured-logging helper that accepts only allow-listed, content-free fields. Every session and grading endpoint then logs through it. - **Plan phase:** 1, Foundation & access. It must merge before any session endpoint (#31). - **Satisfies:** RC-03, RC-06 - **Constrained by:** PA-3, AG-2, AG-3, AG-7 ## Implementation Requirements - [ ] Add a shared Python logging module that follows the package layout of the existing `services/accounts` code. It emits structured JSON for Cloud Logging. - [ ] The helper accepts only allow-listed fields: event name, request ID, opaque session ID, scenario ID and version, status code, duration, and error class or stable error code. It drops unknown fields and never emits them. - [ ] Exceptions are logged by class and stable code. Never log `str(exc)`, request bodies or tracebacks that can carry request data. - [ ] FastAPI exception handlers return the generic error envelope and never echo input. - [ ] Request and response body logging stays off at API Gateway and Cloud Run. Check the settings in `infra/`. - [ ] `services/accounts` adopts the helper wherever it logs today. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A unit test shows that a log call carrying a non-allow-listed field (for example `transcript` or `text`) does not emit that field's value. - [ ] An error-path test shows that an exception whose message contains a synthetic turn produces a log line without the turn text. - [ ] A test or plan check confirms that request and response body logging is disabled for the gateway and the Cloud Run services. - [ ] A repository check flags `print` calls or root-logger calls in service request handlers. ## Visual Context Backend only. SDD Fig. 1 (system architecture). ## Dependencies - Blocked by #18. - Blocks #66 (the session handoff contract) and #31. ## Non-goals - The end-to-end no-persistence proof across storage, client logs and crash reports. #39 owns it. - Analytics and crash reporting. None are added (AG-3). ## Testing Unit tests for the helper and the exception handlers. Use synthetic content only. ## Guardrails AG-2, AG-3, AG-7

items.title: tooling: Chief of staff, one worker and one reviewer agent; role guides and helper duties as skills
items.description: ### Type enhancement ### Summary Build the one agent the owner talks to, in the leaner form he chose on 2026-11-06: a chief of staff that runs as the main session, hands each Ready issue to one temporary worker in its own worktree, and starts a fresh reviewer for each pull request. There are no standing helpers and no agent per role. The helpers' duties become procedures in the chief of staff's skill, and the twelve role guides become skills a worker loads. This waits for the knowledge layer (#712). ### Problem The owner wants one agent to talk to, without managing sessions himself. The first plan added four helper agents and kept twelve role agents. The twelve role agent files differ only in which role guide they point to, and the research found no evidence that a standing manager layer improves results, while every extra agent costs tokens and loses context at each handoff (sources on #721 and in the operating model). ### Proposed fix 1. **Chief of staff agent**, run as the main session on the strongest model. It may not edit code, push or merge (use `disallowedTools` on the agent, not a repository-wide deny, because workers still merge their own reviewed pull requests). It may start only the worker and the reviewer. 2. **`chief-of-staff` skill** (in `.agents/skills/`, with the Claude Code pointer). It holds: - the start-of-session routine: list the owner's open questions (oldest first, at most seven, one line each), then propose the next batch; - **groom**: write or rewrite an issue at high effort so a worker can follow it without guessing; - **overlap check**: compare Files likely touched, the shared hot spots and blockers before every claim; - **review depth**: look the level up in the scrutiny table; it is a lookup, not an agent; - **dispatch brief**: the objective, what done means, which role guides and knowledge notes to load, the files it may touch and the ones it must not. 3. **One worker agent** that replaces the twelve role agent files: the standard model at medium effort, its own worktree, one issue. It loads the role guides its brief names. The brief names them because instructions an agent has to choose to open are often skipped ([Vercel](https://vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals)). 4. **Role guides as skills.** Each guide in `docs/roles/` can be loaded by name, from one source that both Claude Code and Codex read. 5. **One reviewer agent**: a new session with no memory of the change, given only the pull request

items.title: Deep Learning-based Trajectory Prediction
items.description: # Algorithm/Conceptual basis LSTM-GRU Encoder-Decoder Network for Multi-Vehicle Trajectory Prediction # Description & Application This deep learning model forecasts the future behaviors of surrounding vehicles by utilizing a recurrent neural network, more specifically LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) and GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) networks. Taking the input as a historical state trajectory data (position, velocity, acceleration), the model is then required to predict future positions over a prediction horizon (typically 3-5 seconds). The encoder-decoder architecture deals with temporal sequences: the encoder that extracts the features out of previous trajectories and a decoder which produces predictions on future ones. Further, an attention mechanism can be used to capture the vehicle's interactions and determine which other vehicles affect the target vehicle's trajectory more. This is essential for self-driving cars to predict and respond to the action of traffic participants in their vicinity. # Plan for Implementation 1. **Data Generation/Collection:** - Simulate or use real highway trajectory datasets (NGSIM, HighD) - Generate synthetic multi-vehicle scenarios with various maneuvers 2. **Data Preprocessing:** - Extract features: position (x, y), velocity (vx, vy), acceleration (ax, ay), heading - Normalize/standardize trajectory data - Create sliding window sequences (observation window: 3s, prediction horizon: 5s) 3. **Model Architecture:** - **LSTM Encoder:** Process historical trajectory sequences - **GRU Decoder:** Generate future trajectory predictions - **Attention Layer:** Model vehicle interactions (optional) - **Fully Connected Output:** Map to predicted coordinates 4. **Training:** - Loss function: Mean Squared Error (MSE) or Mean Absolute Error (MAE) - Optimizer: Adam with learning rate scheduling - Validation: K-fold cross-validation 5. **Comparative Analysis:** Implement and compare vanilla RNN, LSTM, GRU, Bi-LSTM models 6. **Visualization:** Plot predicted vs. actual trajectories, attention weights, error distributions # References in Consideration 1. Kaouther Messaoud, Itheri Yahiaoui, Anne Verroust-Blondet, Fawzi Nashashibi, "Attention Based Vehicle Trajectory Prediction. IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers", In press, 10.1109/TIV.2020.2991952. hal-02543967 https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341055264_Attention_Based_Vehicle_Trajectory_Prediction 2. Jiaqin Wang, Kai Liu, Hantao

items.title: [Feature Request] Improve Hybrid A* with Reeds-Shepp Paths and Reversing Support
items.description: **Description** Currently, the existing sample code of Hybrid A* Path Planning doesn't support reversing movement. To make it more practical and professional -- similar to those used in autonomous valet parking -- we need to upgrade the heuristic and the motion model. I would like to propose an enhancement to the Hybrid A* algorithm by integrating the Reeds-Shepp curves. **Tasks** - Integration of Reeds-Shepp Paths: Use Reeds-Shepp curves as the analytic expansion (shot-to-goal) to improve search efficiency and path quality. - Support for Reversing: Update the motion model to allow the vehicle to move to backward. - Direction Change Penalty: Implement a cost function that penalizes switching between forward and backward to ensure smooth paths. - Heuristic Update: Improve the heuristic considering the non-holonomic constraints. **Reference Code** [Current version of Hybrid A* Global Path Planning](https://github.com/ShisatoYano/AutonomousVehicleControlBeginnersGuide/tree/main/src/simulations/path_planning/astar_hybrid_path_planning)

items.title: Photo map: browse your photostream by location
items.description: A map view of the user's photos by location. - Request location as an extra field on the photo lists the app already loads (confirm in a small spike). If the Tag Browser's library scan (#93) exists, collect location in the same scan. - Pins and clusters; click a cluster to open those photos in the normal grid; draw or zoom to an area and use "Download N shown". - Existing filters (privacy, license, tags, date) narrow the pins. - Show how many photos have a location ("N of M"). - The Archive tab (#98) could show the same map from GPS embedded in files. **Decision needed: map tiles.** A map needs background images from a provider (OpenStreetMap-based or paid), which means the app contacts a third party; the README must be updated, and OSM's free tile server has usage limits, so a released app may need a provider key. Leaning toward online tiles, disclosed in the README. **Also:** a map library (e.g. Leaflet) is a new dependency; ask before adding. Private photos appear on the map for the owner; keep in mind for screenshots. Related: #93, #97, #98. **Depends on:** Decision on map tiles (online provider vs bundled offline map)

items.title: Fix an all-layers composite render budget for run:board on the stress fixture
items.description: ## 概要 **「`run:board` のライブ画面で、全エフェクトを同時に出したときの描画コストがテストで固定されておらず、描画の外でメインスレッドが止まる時間はどこにも出ない」**という kit の課題です。描画方式を作り替える前に、今のコストを一つの予算テストにし、実ボードの引っ掛かりを `--timing` で見えるようにします。 1. 今の予算テストは、スピナー、雨、リビール、ワイプを一つずつ測っています。2. 実際の画面では、テーマのエフェクトがすべて同時に動きます。3. 全部が重なったときの 1 秒分の描画時間は、どのテストにも出ません。4. `--timing` が計るのは描画(`tick draw` / `turn draw`)と 200 ms 以上の停止だけで、描画の外の処理と 200 ms 未満の遅れは出ません。 今まで困らなかったのは、エフェクトが少なかったからです。テーマが増えて画面が賑やかになり、重さが目に見えるようになりました。この後の作り替えで「速くなったか」「遅くなっていないか」「引っ掛かりが消えたか」を判断するには、全レイヤー同時の基準と、実ボードの遅れの基準が先に要ります。 直し方: 負荷用の大きな盤面(160x50)に全テーマのエフェクトを同時に載せ、1 秒分の描画にかかる時間と書き込み回数を、テーマごとの予算テストにします。あわせて `--timing` に、起床の遅れ、停止の時刻、`redraw` 段階の描画以外の時間を足し、3 テーマの実ボードの値を基準として残します。 ## 背景 - 種別: 非不具合 - 目的: 機能改善 - 人の判断: 不要 - 規模見積もり: 約 8 ファイル / 400 行(テスト含む) - 分割しない理由: 分けられない — 予算テストと `--timing` の追加は、どちらも「作り替えの前の基準」で、後の子(#8826)が両方を緑・悪化なしで通すことを条件にする。片方だけでは作り替えの可否を判定できない エピックの最初の子です。後に続く「セル格子とフレームループ」の子は、このテストを緑のまま通すことを条件にします。 調査済みの現状(描画の中): | # | 原因の候補 | 場所 | |---|---|---| | 1 | エフェクトごとに違う周期の最小値で起きる | `scripts/run/board/run-board-spin.ts` の `next_turn` | | 2 | 1 回の起床で最大約 9 回、別々の同期ブロックで書く | `scripts/run/board/run-board-spin-turn.ts` の `write_turn` | | 3 | 毎秒の再描画で全行を消して書き直し、`spun()` が文字列を何度も走査する | `scripts/run/board/run-board-screen.ts`、`scripts/run/board/run-board-spin.ts` | | 4 | パネルは 50 ms ごとに全セルの Map を 2 回作る。ジャンプは端末の全セルを毎回回す | `scripts/run/board/run-board-panel-draw.ts`、`scripts/run/board/run-board-jump-screen.ts` | どれが支配的かは分かっていません。`--timing`(`scripts/run/board/run-board-timing.ts`)は draw を `tick` / `turn` で分けて計ります。 調査済みの現状(描画の外、2026-11-24): 実ボードの実測(matrix、160x50、25 秒、`pnpm josh run:board --timing --theme matrix`、エフェクトがほぼ動いていない盤面): | 項目 | 値 | |---|---| | `tick draw` | 中央値 7.7 ms、最大 40.4 ms(25 回) | | `turn draw` | 中央値 0.1 ms、最大 1.6 ms(316 回) | | 200 ms 以上の停止 | 1 回、441.7 ms、段階は `redraw`、GC は 4.3 ms | | CPU | 25 秒中 16.2 秒 | | ヒープの最大 | メイン 71.4 MB、ワーカー 336.6 MB | 441.7 ms のうち約 400 ms は、描画でも GC でもありません。メインスレッドで描画のタイマーの外にある処理は次のとおりです。どれが止めたかは分かっていません。 | # | 候補 | 場所 | |---|---|---| | 5 | 起動から最初の `turn` までは、モジュールの読み込み、ワーカーの起動、イントロとリビールの描画がすべて `redraw` に数えられる | `scripts/run/board/run-board-stall.ts` の `FIRST_STAGE`、`scripts/run/board/run-board-live.ts` の `revealed_tick` | | 6 | 音の `cached_wav` は呼ばれるたびに、キャッシュに当たってもソース 2 本を `readFileSync` して sha256 を取る。外れると WAV を同期で合成して書く | `scripts/run/board/run-board-sound-wav.ts` の `file_name_of` / `implementation_digest` | | 7 | ワーカーは plan 全体と `display` を毎回 post し、メインが受信のたびに複製を受け取る。大きさは未計測 | `scripts/run/board/run-board-data.ts` の `DataPost`、`scripts/ru

items.title: Ask HN: Are startups today worth it even in a best case scenario?
items.description: I'm gonna open this with the disclaimer that this is purely a financial and risk comparison post. No one is complaining that we are poorly compensated. It is good to discuss compensation so we can make informed and educated decisions when deciding how to commit the next few years of our lives. A close friend of mine joined an AI startup (being intentionally vague) around 1.5 years ago and despite the company doing extremely well on valuation, I'm surprised at how he's not really better off than just working at a large tech company. Concrete numbers for the startup: -200k salary -Equity grant over 4 years is 500k -The company's valuation has since went from single billions to tens of billions, leaving him with a 10x multiplier when looking only at valuation. After you account for dilution, it's closer to 6x. -Liquidity event annually allows you to sell 10% of your vested shares Big tech at a similar years of experience is around 400-500k total comp, and the RSU component is generally liquid. For example sake and ease of calculation, if you assume that my friend's entire equity was vested, and he was able to sell 10% of it, it would amount to approximately $300k/liquidity event, which brings him to around 500k a year as well (200k + 300k). In reality, he's really only able to access $300k/4 since that's all he has vested and that brings him closer to $75k for this liquidity event. There are a lot of variables I'm leaving out obviously such as potential future value, IPO, etc., but the thing that is surprising to me overall is that this is a close to best case outcome, yet the employee doesn't really end up any better off than big tech due to lack of liquidity and dilution. I mean I get it, impact, interesting work, etc. -- the qualitative measures -- aren't really accounted for, but I'm not looking to make a wholistic comparison. This brings me to the question: Is the risk in a startup ever justified for a lower level employee (engineer, Product Manager, Program Manager, etc.)?

items.title: Ask HN: Should Uber Ratings Decay over Time?
items.description: I’ve been thinking about how platforms like Uber calculate reputation scores, and I believe there’s a fundamental flaw in how historical ratings are treated. Uber calculates passenger ratings using the last 500 rated trips, regardless of when those trips occurred. In my case, I have 455 ratings, 426 of which are five stars (93.6%). My overall rating is 4.86. What bothers me isn’t the score itself, but the underlying methodology. A negative rating from five years ago can carry exactly the same weight as one received yesterday. And if you’re an infrequent user who hasn’t accumulated 500 ratings, that negative feedback could influence your reputation for years. This raises an interesting question: Should reputation systems measure your historical average, or should they attempt to represent who you are today? One possible solution is exponential time decay: Weight = 2^(-t/H) Where t is the age of the rating and H is a half-life, perhaps 12 months. Under that approach, a rating from one year ago would carry 50% of its original weight, and one from two years ago just 25%. Of course, this introduces other challenges. How do you prevent someone with a history of poor behaviour from simply waiting for their reputation to recover? How do you maintain statistical confidence for infrequent users? Would Bayesian smoothing or a minimum effective sample size help? There’s also a broader philosophical question around the right to be forgotten. Should digital reputation systems indefinitely preserve the consequences of historical assessments, particularly when those assessments are subjective and potentially no longer representative? I’m curious how others would approach this. * Is a rolling window of 500 ratings statistically defensible without considering time? * Would exponential decay produce a fairer and more predictive reputation score? * Should platforms expose both a lifetime rating and a recent-behaviour rating? * Are there better approaches already being used in other reputation systems? I’d be particularly interested in perspectives from people who’ve worked on marketplace ranking, trust and safety, or reputation algorithms. It seems like a relatively simple mathematical change, but one with potentially significant implications for fairness across digital platforms.
